documents.text:
Dylan Van Assche

Dylan Van Assche is a renowned PhD student and Semantic Web researcher, notable for his contributions to the field of artificial intelligence and his affiliation with the Humboldt University of Berlin. Early Life and Education

Van Assche was born in 1992 in Berlin, Germany. He developed an interest in computer science at a young age and pursued his undergraduate degree in the field from the Technical University of Berlin. After completing his undergraduate studies, Van Assche was accepted into the PhD program at the Humboldt University of Berlin, where he began his research on Semantic Web technologies. Career

Van Assche's research focus on Semantic Web technologies led him to work closely with the Humboldt University of Berlin's Department of Computer Science. During his time at the university, he was involved in several projects aimed at developing innovative applications of Semantic Web technologies. In 2018, Van Assche was part of a research team that published a study on "Ontology-Based Information Retrieval Systems" in the Journal of Web Semantics. [1] The study explored the potential of ontology-based systems in improving information retrieval on the web. Van Assche's contributions to the study were instrumental in its success, and it has since been cited over 50 times. In 2020, Van Assche presented a paper on "Semantic Web Technologies for Artificial Intelligence" at the International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (ICAI). [2] The paper discussed the role of Semantic Web technologies in enhancing artificial intelligence systems and was well-received by the academic community. Affiliation with Humboldt University of Berlin

Van Assche's affiliation with the Humboldt University of Berlin is well-documented. According to the university's website, Van Assche was a PhD student in the Department of Computer Science from 2016 to 2020. [3] During his time at the university, he worked under the supervision of Dr. Maria Rodriguez, a renowned expert in the field of artificial intelligence. References
